note: Desserts, scored honestly. A tiramisu is a tiramisu and the app does not pretend otherwise — it shows the numbers and says plainly that this one is for a birthday. A few here happen to be built on fruit, yogurt and nuts and score well without trying; the rest are worth every gram and say so.

recipes.title: Tiramisu
recipes.blurb: No baking, no oven, thirty minutes plus a night in the fridge. The two things that matter: hard savoiardi, and a dip in the coffee measured in seconds.
steps: Whisk the yolks and sugar in a bowl set over barely simmering water for 6-8 minutes, until pale, thick and hot to the touch — about 160°F. This is a zabaglione, and cooking the yolks is what makes the dessert safe as well as stable.
Cool it 10 minutes, then beat in the mascarpone until smooth. Do not overbeat; mascarpone splits.
Whip the cream to soft peaks with the vanilla and fold it in, in three additions.
Dip each ladyfinger in the coffee for one second a side. One. They go on absorbing for twenty minutes afterward, and a soggy tiramisu is always an over-dipped one.
Layer: biscuits, half the cream, biscuits, the rest of the cream. Smooth the top.
Refrigerate at least 6 hours, ideally overnight. Dust thickly with cocoa immediately before serving — cocoa dusted early turns to mud.
recipes.kidTweak: Make a small dish with strong hot chocolate instead of coffee. It works, and it is a genuinely good children's dessert.
recipes.restaurantTouch: A pinch of salt in the cream. Every rich dessert improves with it and nobody can identify why.
recipes.leftovers: Keeps 3 days and is best on day two. It does not freeze.
recipes.heartNote: Mascarpone and heavy cream make this one of the richest things in the collection — the app scores it accordingly and it is not wrong. It is a birthday dessert for ten people, and at that size it is entirely reasonable.

recipes.title: Apple Tarte Tatin
recipes.blurb: Apples caramelized in the pan, pastry laid over the top, baked and flipped. The most impressive thing you can make from four ingredients, and it is genuinely not hard.
steps: Toss the apple halves with lemon juice. Use a firm apple — Honeycrisp, Braeburn, Northern Spy. A McIntosh will dissolve.

Melt the butter and sugar in the skillet over medium heat and cook, swirling but not stirring, 6-8 minutes until it turns amber. Caramel is done by color, not by time, and it goes from amber to burnt in about twenty seconds.
Off the heat, add the vanilla and salt, then pack the apple halves in tightly, rounded side down, in concentric circles. They shrink, so tighter than looks right.
Cook over medium-low 15 minutes, basting the tops with the caramel a few times.
Lay the pastry over, tuck the edges down inside the pan, cut three steam vents, and bake at 400°F for 28-32 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and puffed.
Rest exactly 5 minutes — no more, or the caramel sets and glues it in. Put a plate over the pan and flip in one committed motion, away from yourself. It is hot caramel; use oven mitts and mean it.
recipes.kidTweak: Serve with cold plain yogurt or ice cream. The contrast is most of the pleasure.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Amber, not gold. An underdone caramel gives you a sweet tart; a proper one gives you a bitter edge that makes the whole thing taste like something.
recipes.leftovers: Keeps 2 days at room temperature. Reheat in a 350°F oven to re-crisp the pastry.

recipes.title: Olive Oil and Citrus Cake
recipes.blurb: One bowl, no mixer, and it keeps for four days getting better. Olive oil cakes stay moist in a way butter cakes cannot.

ingredients.prep: zest of both, juice of one

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Line and oil a 9-inch pan.

Rub the citrus zest into the sugar with your fingertips for a minute until the sugar is damp and smells like an orange grove. This releases the oils in a way that stirring never does, and it is the single best trick in citrus baking.
Whisk in the eggs, then the olive oil in a steady stream, then the yogurt, juice and vanilla.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt until just combined. Stop while a few streaks remain.
Bake 40-45 minutes until a skewer comes out with a crumb or two. The top should be deep gold and cracked.
Cool in the pan 10 minutes, then turn out. Dust with powdered sugar. Use a fruity, decent olive oil — you will taste it, and that is the point.
recipes.kidTweak: Bake it in a muffin tin for 18 minutes for lunchbox portions.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Zest rubbed into sugar. Thirty seconds of work for twice the citrus flavor.
recipes.leftovers: Better on day two. Keeps 4 days covered at room temperature; freezes well.
recipes.heartNote: Three-quarters of a cup of olive oil rather than butter means this dessert has almost no saturated fat — about 2 g a slice against 9 or 10 for a butter cake.

recipes.title: Dark Chocolate Avocado Mousse
recipes.blurb: Ten minutes in a blender, no cooking, no eggs. Nobody guesses the avocado — it is there for texture, and the cocoa and real chocolate do the rest.
steps: The avocados have to be properly ripe — any firmness leaves a green note and a lumpy texture.
Blend the avocado, cocoa, maple, oat milk, vanilla and salt until completely smooth, scraping down twice. Give it longer than you think; two full minutes.
Melt the chocolate gently and blend it in last. Real chocolate rather than cocoa alone is what gives the mousse body as it chills.
Chill at least an hour. It firms considerably.
Serve in small cups with raspberries and pistachios. Small — it is rich.
recipes.kidTweak: Do not tell them until after. Then tell them, because it is a good trick.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Half a teaspoon of salt in a chocolate dessert. It is more than feels right and it is what makes the chocolate taste dark rather than sweet.
recipes.leftovers: Keeps 3 days pressed with wrap. The surface can darken slightly; stir it.
recipes.heartNote: A genuinely good-scoring dessert: the fat is avocado and cocoa butter, the sweetener is maple, and a serving carries about 7 g of fiber.
recipes.allergenNote: Contains tree nut; the chocolate may contain dairy.

recipes.title: Blueberry Buckle
recipes.blurb: New England's summer cake: a tender crumb, more blueberries than batter, and a cinnamon streusel that sinks in and makes the top buckle.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Make the streusel first: rub 1/3 cup of the flour, the brown sugar, cinnamon and 2 tablespoons of the butter together with your fingers into coarse crumbs. Chill it.
Cream the remaining butter with the granulated sugar and lemon zest for 3 minutes until pale and fluffy. That aeration is the cake's lift.
Beat in the egg and vanilla, then alternate the remaining flour (with the baking powder and salt) and the buttermilk, in three additions, starting and ending with flour.
Toss the blueberries with a tablespoon of flour and fold them in gently. The flour is what keeps them suspended instead of sinking.
Spread in the pan, scatter the streusel over, and bake 45-50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean and the middle no longer wobbles.
Cool at least 20 minutes. Buckle is better warm than hot.
recipes.kidTweak: It is cake with fruit in it and crumbs on top. There is no tweak needed.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Lemon zest creamed into the butter and sugar. It makes the blueberries taste more like blueberries.
recipes.leftovers: Keeps 3 days covered. Excellent for breakfast, which is what a buckle is really for.

recipes.title: Banana Pudding
recipes.blurb: A real stovetop custard rather than a box of instant, layered with wafers and bananas and left overnight to go soft. Southern potluck royalty.
steps: Whisk the sugar, cornstarch and salt in a saucepan, then whisk in the milk gradually so there are no lumps. Cook over medium, whisking constantly, until it thickens and just bubbles, about 8 minutes.
Temper the yolks: whisk a cup of the hot mixture into the beaten yolks, then pour it all back into the pan. Cook 2 minutes more, whisking hard. Skipping the tempering gives you sweet scrambled eggs.
Off the heat, whisk in the butter and vanilla. Strain it through a sieve — a thirty-second insurance policy against any lumps.
Layer in the dish: custard, wafers, bananas, repeating and finishing with custard. Press wrap onto the surface and chill 4 hours or overnight.
Before serving, whip the cream with the powdered sugar to soft peaks and spread it over. The wafers should have gone completely soft — that is the whole point and it takes the full four hours.
recipes.kidTweak: Assemble it in individual jars and let each child layer their own.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Strain the custard. Every professional pastry kitchen does it and it takes half a minute.
recipes.leftovers: Keeps 2 days; the bananas darken. Make it the day before, not two.
recipes.heartNote: Four yolks and a cup of cream across ten servings — a proper dessert, honestly scored. Made with 1% milk rather than whole it is meaningfully lighter than the classic and no worse for it.

recipes.title: Flan
recipes.blurb: Caramel in the bottom of the dish, a custard poured over, baked in a water bath and inverted. Five ingredients and the most elegant dessert in Latin America.
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Melt the sugar in a dry pan over medium heat without stirring — swirl it — until it is deep amber, 7-9 minutes. Pour it straight into the cake pan and tilt to coat the bottom. It sets hard in seconds; that is fine.
Blend or whisk the condensed milk, milk, eggs, vanilla, salt and zest until smooth. Do not aerate it — bubbles become holes in the set custard.
Strain the custard over the caramel.
Set the pan inside a roasting pan and pour hot water halfway up its sides. The water bath is what keeps the custard from curdling at the edges.
Bake 50-60 minutes until the center wobbles as a single mass rather than rippling.
Chill at least 4 hours, ideally overnight. Run a knife around the edge, put a rimmed plate over the top, and invert — the caramel has liquefied into a sauce and it pours out over the top.
recipes.kidTweak: It is a wobbly caramel custard, which is a universally popular category. Serve small.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Overnight in the fridge. A flan turned out after four hours is good; after twelve, the caramel has fully dissolved into sauce and it is a different dessert.
recipes.leftovers: Keeps 3 days and stays good the whole time.

recipes.title: Mango Sticky Rice
recipes.blurb: Thailand's great dessert: warm coconut-sweetened glutinous rice, cold ripe mango, salted coconut cream poured over. Steaming the rice properly is the whole thing.
equipment: steamer or fine sieve over a pot

ingredients.prep: or Thai glutinous rice, soaked 4 hours

steps: Soak the rice at least 4 hours, or overnight. True Thai glutinous rice is worth seeking out; short-grain sushi rice is the closest common substitute.
Steam the drained rice over simmering water for 25 minutes, lined with cheesecloth or a fine sieve, until translucent and chewy. Boiling it gives you porridge.
Warm three-quarters of the coconut milk with the sugar and half a teaspoon of salt until dissolved — do not boil it.
Pour that over the hot rice, stir once, cover, and leave 20 minutes. It looks far too wet and it drinks all of it.

For the topping, simmer the remaining coconut milk with the cornstarch and the last quarter teaspoon of salt for 2 minutes until slightly thickened. It should taste distinctly salty against the sweet rice — that contrast is the dish.
Serve warm rice with cold mango, the salted cream poured over, and sesame seeds.
recipes.kidTweak: Sweet sticky rice with mango is close to universally liked. Serve small portions; it is rich.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Salt in the coconut topping. Without it the dessert is flat and sugary; with it, it is one of the great sweet-salty combinations.
recipes.leftovers: The rice hardens cold. Steam it again 5 minutes to bring it back. Best the day it is made.
recipes.heartNote: Full-fat coconut milk is very high in saturated fat. This is a real dessert for a special occasion, not a weeknight pudding.

recipes.title: Affogato
recipes.blurb: A scoop of something cold, a shot of hot espresso poured over. Two ingredients, ninety seconds, and it ends a dinner party better than anything you could bake.
steps: For the frozen yogurt version: stir the maple into the yogurt, freeze it in a shallow container for 3 hours, and scrape it into scoops. Or use good vanilla ice cream and skip this.
Chill four small glasses. A cold glass buys you thirty seconds before it becomes a milkshake.
Put a scoop in each glass. Pull the espresso and pour it over at the table, in front of people.
Shaved chocolate and hazelnuts on top. Eat it immediately — the whole appeal is the moment when it is half melted.
recipes.kidTweak: Hot chocolate instead of espresso works and is a real dessert in its own right.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Pour it at the table. There is a small theater to affogato and it costs nothing.
recipes.heartNote: Frozen Greek yogurt instead of ice cream cuts the saturated fat by roughly two-thirds and adds about 10 g of protein a serving.

recipes.title: Air Fryer Apple Hand Pies
recipes.blurb: Puff pastry, spiced apple, twelve minutes in the air fryer. Warm hand pies on a weeknight without heating the oven or frying anything.
steps: Cook the diced apple with the butter, brown sugar, spices, lemon and salt over medium for 6 minutes until softened. Stir in the cornstarch slurried with a teaspoon of water and cook 1 minute more.
Cool the filling completely. Warm filling melts pastry and you get leaks.
Cut the pastry into 8 rectangles. Put a heaped tablespoon of filling on half of each, fold over, and seal the edges with a fork pressed hard.
Cut two small vents in each top, brush with egg, sprinkle with granulated sugar.
Air fry at 350°F for 11-13 minutes until deep golden and puffed. Lower and slower than most air fryer recipes — pastry needs time for its layers to separate.
Cool 10 minutes. The filling is molten and it will burn a mouth.
recipes.kidTweak: Sealing the edges with a fork is a good job for small hands, and they are more careful about it than adults.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Vents in the top. Without them the steam blows a hole in the side and the filling ends up in the basket.
recipes.leftovers: Keeps 2 days. Re-crisp for 3 minutes at 350°F.

recipes.title: Air Fryer Churros
recipes.blurb: A real choux paste piped, air fried and rolled in cinnamon sugar, with a proper chocolate sauce for dipping. Thirty minutes, no vat of oil.
equipment: piping bag with a star tip
steps: Bring 1 cup water, the butter, salt and 1 tablespoon of the sugar to a boil. Dump in the flour all at once and stir hard over the heat for 2 minutes until it forms a smooth ball that leaves a film on the pan bottom.
Cool 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time and the vanilla. It will look broken after each egg and come back together — keep beating.
Pipe 5-inch lengths through a large star tip straight into the air fryer basket, lined with perforated paper. The ridges from the star tip are structural: they give the churro its crisp edges.
Mist with oil and air fry at 375°F for 10-12 minutes until golden and firm.
Toss the hot churros in the remaining sugar mixed with the cinnamon.
Sauce: warm the milk and pour it over the chopped chocolate, then stir until glossy. Spanish chocolate for churros is thick enough to coat — it is a dipping sauce, not a drink.
recipes.kidTweak: Piping is the fun part. Let them do it and accept the shapes.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Sugar them while they are hot. Cold churros will not hold the coating.
recipes.leftovers: Eat immediately — this is genuinely a to-order dessert.

recipes.title: Kheer (Cardamom Rice Pudding)
recipes.blurb: Rice simmered slowly in milk until it thickens on its own, scented with cardamom and saffron and finished with pistachios. No eggs, no thickener, no rush.
steps: Bring the milk to a simmer with the rice in a heavy pan. Heavy matters — thin pans scorch milk and there is no recovering from that taste.

Simmer 40-45 minutes on low, stirring every five minutes and scraping the bottom, until the rice has broken down and the milk has reduced by about a third. The starch from the rice is the only thickener.
Crush the saffron and steep it in a tablespoon of warm milk, then stir it in with the sugar, cardamom and salt in the last 10 minutes. Sugar added early slows the rice down.
Stir in most of the nuts and the raisins.
Serve warm or cold — both are correct, and it thickens considerably in the fridge. Top with the remaining pistachios.
recipes.kidTweak: Rice pudding is rice pudding. Serve warm with a little extra milk poured over.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Scrape the bottom every time you stir. The caramelized milk solids down there are flavor if they are incorporated and ruin if they are left to burn.
recipes.leftovers: Keeps 4 days and thickens to a spoonable pudding. Loosen with milk.
recipes.heartNote: Made with 1% milk this is about 200 calories a serving with 8 g of protein — one of the lighter desserts here, and it does not taste like a compromise.

recipes.title: Strawberry Shortcake
recipes.blurb: Real biscuits, not sponge cake — flaky, barely sweet, split and filled with macerated berries and lightly whipped cream. June, on a plate.
steps: Toss the strawberries with half the sugar and the lemon juice and leave them at room temperature at least 30 minutes. They collapse slightly and make their own syrup — that syrup is the sauce.

Heat the oven to 425°F. Grate the frozen butter into the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and 2 tablespoons of the sugar. Grating frozen butter gives you flakier biscuits than cutting it in, with a fraction of the work.
Stir in the buttermilk until it just holds together. Pat it out, fold it in thirds twice — those folds are the layers — and cut eight rounds.
Bake 14-16 minutes until risen and golden. Do not twist the cutter; a twisted edge seals and the biscuit rises lopsided.
Whip the cream with the remaining sugar and vanilla to soft peaks. Stop while it still slumps.
Split the warm biscuits, spoon berries and syrup over the bottoms, add cream, and lean the tops on at an angle.
recipes.kidTweak: Let them mash a few of the berries with a fork. More syrup, and it makes them part of it.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Soft peaks, not stiff. Cream whipped to stiff peaks is a frosting; cream at soft peaks folds into the berry syrup on the plate.
recipes.leftovers: Biscuits keep a day. Assemble to order — this dessert has a fifteen-minute window and that is part of its charm.
recipes.garden: June strawberries from a local patch make a version of this that supermarket berries cannot touch. It is worth planning the month around.

recipes.title: Walnut Pistachio Baklava
recipes.blurb: Forty layers of phyllo, nuts and butter, cut before baking and drenched in lemon-honey syrup after. A Saturday project that keeps for two weeks.
steps: Make the syrup first and let it cool completely: simmer 1 cup of the sugar with 1 cup water, the honey, a strip of lemon peel and the juice for 10 minutes. Cold syrup onto hot pastry is the rule — the reverse gives you a soggy tray.
Pulse the nuts with the remaining sugar, cinnamon, cloves and salt to a coarse crumb, not a powder.
Keep the phyllo stack under a damp towel while you work; exposed sheets shatter within a minute.

Butter the pan. Lay 10 sheets, brushing every second one with butter. Spread a third of the nuts. Repeat with 8 sheets and nuts, twice more, then finish with 14 sheets on top, buttering more generously as you go.
Cut all the way through into diamonds before baking. Baked baklava cannot be cut without shattering.
Bake at 325°F for 70-80 minutes until deep golden all the way through. Slow is essential — the middle layers need to dry out and crisp.
Pour the cold syrup over the hot pastry the moment it comes out. It will hiss and sizzle for a full minute. Leave it uncovered at least 6 hours before eating; overnight is better.
recipes.kidTweak: Brushing butter on phyllo is a genuinely satisfying job and children are patient with it for longer than you would expect.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Cold syrup, hot pastry. That temperature difference is what lets the syrup soak in without softening the layers.
recipes.leftovers: Two weeks at room temperature, loosely covered. Never refrigerate it — it goes gluey.
recipes.heartNote: Twenty-four small pieces, three cups of nuts and twelve tablespoons of butter. Cut it small — one diamond is a portion, and that is how it is served across the Levant and Greece.
recipes.allergenNote: Contains wheat, dairy and tree nut.

recipes.title: Northwest Berry Hazelnut Crisp
recipes.blurb: Blackberries and raspberries under an oat and hazelnut topping. Cornstarch and a long enough bake are what keep the fruit from flooding the dish.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Toss the berries with the granulated sugar, cornstarch and the zest and juice of the lemon. Cornstarch is what turns berry juice into sauce instead of soup.
Rub the oats, hazelnuts, flour, brown sugar, cinnamon, salt and cold butter together with your fingers until it clumps in pieces the size of peas and hazelnuts.
Scatter the topping over the fruit without pressing it down — a packed topping steams instead of crisping.
Bake 40-45 minutes until the topping is deep gold and the fruit is bubbling thickly at the edges. Bubbling is the doneness cue; a crisp pulled before the fruit boils will be runny.
Cool at least 20 minutes so the juices set. Serve warm with yogurt or ice cream.
recipes.kidTweak: Frozen berries work straight from the freezer — add 10 minutes to the bake and do not thaw them first.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Toast and skin the hazelnuts before they go in the topping. Raw hazelnut in a crisp tastes like nothing.
recipes.leftovers: Keeps 3 days. The topping softens; re-crisp it in a 350°F oven for 10 minutes.
recipes.garden: Blackberries and raspberries both thrive in zone 6a and a few canes will supply this all August.
recipes.allergenNote: Contains tree nut, wheat and dairy.
